title: Point masses of a probability density
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\phi$ be a nonnegative function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube whose uniform expectation is $1$, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. The associated probability mass function assigns to $x$ the mass $\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\phi(x)/2^n\right)$, where $\operatorname{ofReal}$ is the standard map from nonnegative real numbers to nonnegative extended real numbers.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a point of the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
